chapters.summary: Council staff call the meeting to order, welcome attendees to the New York City Council Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and instruct the public not to approach the dais and to silence all electronics before turning the floor over to the Chair.
chapters.title: Council staff opens Transportation and Infrastructure hearing and gives housekeeping instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to the New York City Council vote on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please do not approach the dais and silence all electronics.

chapters.summary: Chair Shaun Abreu welcomes attendees to the hearing and announces that the committee will vote on Proposed Intro No. 202-A, sponsored by Council Member Gutiérrez, relating to the time permitted for installation of covered safety treatments on streets adjacent to schools.
chapters.title: Chair Shaun Abreu opens the hearing and announces the vote on Intro 202-A

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's hearing of the New York City Council's Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Sean O'Brien, Majority Leader and Chair of this committee.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: At today's hearing, the committee will vote on the following legislation.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: 202A, sponsored by Councilmember Gutierrez, in relation to the time permitted for the installation of covered safety treatments on any portion of a street adjacent to a school.

chapters.summary: Chair Abreu describes the bill's purpose: ensuring that when DOT performs a traffic study near a school and determines a safety treatment is warranted, the treatment is implemented in a timely and efficient manner.
chapters.title: Abreu explains that Intro 202-A requires timely DOT safety treatment installation near schools

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This bill will help ensure that when DOT performs a traffic study near a school and determines a safety treatment should be implemented, the treatment is implemented in a timely and efficient manner.

chapters.summary: Chair Abreu thanks his staff and committee staff for their work preparing the hearing, naming Jaleesa Quigley, Jake Borey, Sienna Townsend, Theo Miller, Kevin Katowski, John Brazil, and Ye Tuong.
chapters.title: Abreu thanks committee staff by name for preparing the hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Before we begin, I would like to thank my staff and the committee staff for their hard work in preparing for today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Jaleesa Quigley, my Deputy Chief of Staff and Director of Legislation and Budget, Jake Borey.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My senior advisor, Sienna Townsend, senior counsel to the committee, Theo Miller, counsel to the committee, Kevin Katowski and John Brazil, senior policy analyst to the committee, and Ye Tuong, financial analyst to the committee.

chapters.summary: After Abreu yields the floor, Council Member Jennifer Gutiérrez thanks colleagues who signed on to the bill and argues that streets near schools are among the most heavily trafficked in the city, with many children and families not sufficiently safe when crossing.
chapters.title: Gutiérrez opens on unsafe school-zone crossings and heavy traffic near schools

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now allow Councilmember Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: To read her opening statement on her bill.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I want to thank all my colleagues who have already signed on and hope that we can obviously pass this bill today.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Streets near schools are some of the most heavily trafficked areas in the entire city, and we have a problem.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Many kids and families are not sufficiently safe when they're crossing the street at school.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez says that when DOT determines a street near a school needs a traffic calming device, even something as simple as a stop sign or speed bump, installation takes far too long, with families and schools waiting years.
chapters.title: Gutiérrez says families wait years for simple traffic calming devices

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: When DOT determines that a street near a school needs a traffic calming device, even something as simple as a stop sign, that amount of time that it takes for the actual installation in many cases is too damn long.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Many families and schools are waiting years for something as simple as a speed bump, for example.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And this is a matter of life and death.

chapters.summary: Calling the issue a matter of life and death, Gutiérrez cites New York City Open Data motor vehicle collision records showing that since 2021, crashes within a .15-mile radius of a school killed 76 people and injured 27,518.
chapters.title: Gutiérrez cites crash data: 76 killed and 27,518 injured near schools since 2021

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: A study of New York City Open Data's motor vehicle collisions found that since 2021 through today, crashes within a .15 mile radius of a school have killed 76 people and have injured 27,518 people.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez explains that Intro 202 imposes a 120-day time limit for covered safety treatments and a 180-day limit for traffic control signals on any portion of a street adjacent to a school, calling it a simple solution that saves lives.
chapters.title: Gutiérrez details Intro 202's 120-day and 180-day installation deadlines

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: It saves lives by imposing a time limit of 120 days for covered safety treatments and of 180 days for traffic control signals on any portion of a street adjacent to a school.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez says the law is necessary to make school zones safer and to build community confidence that the city prioritizes child safety, arguing faster deployment of traffic calming and control devices keeps preventative measures pace with identified risks, and asks colleagues to pass the bill.
chapters.title: Gutiérrez argues faster deployment builds community confidence in school-zone safety

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Implementing this law is necessary to make school zones safer and build community confidence that the city is prioritizing safety, child safety.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Faster deployment of traffic calming and control devices ensures that preventative measures keep pace with identified risks, directly protecting students and others who travel near schools.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I hope that you can all join me in passing this bill.

chapters.summary: Chair Abreu asks the committee clerk to call the roll, and Clerk William Martin announces a roll call vote on Proposed Introduction 202-A before the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
chapters.title: Abreu directs the committee clerk to call the roll on Intro 202-A

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now ask the committee clerk to call the roll.

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: William Martin, committee clerk, roll call vote, Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, proposed introduction 202A.

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin calls members one by one on Intro 202-A, with Council Members Dinowitz, Louis, Abreu, Brooks-Powers, Hanif, Krishnan, Marte, Justin Sanchez, Wong, and Pierina Ana Sanchez recorded in the affirmative; several members congratulate the sponsor during the call.
chapters.title: Committee clerk William Martin conducts the roll call vote on Intro 202-A

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin announces the result: with 10 votes in the affirmative, 0 in the negative, and no abstentions, Proposed Introduction 202-A has been approved by the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
chapters.title: Intro 202-A approved 10-0-0 by the committee

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: With a vote of 10 in the affirmative, 0 in the negative, and no abstentions, item has been approved by the committee.

chapters.summary: Chair Shaun Abreu declares the vote closed, concluding the committee's business on Intro 202-A.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu closes the vote and adjourns the hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: With that, this vote is closed.

summary: The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure held a hearing and vote on Proposed Intro No. 202-A, sponsored by Council Member Jennifer Gutiérrez, which sets time limits for installing covered safety treatments near schools.

Gutiérrez argued that DOT takes far too long to install traffic calming devices near schools, citing 76 deaths and 27,518 injuries within a .15-mile radius of schools since 2021, and proposed 120-day limits for safety treatments and 180 days for traffic control signals.
The committee voted 10-0-0 to approve the bill, and Chair Shaun Abreu closed the vote.
title: Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure
topic: Time permitted for the installation of covered safety treatments on any portion of a street adjacent to a school
